methods.summary:
Frame smoothing: each frame is presented mixed with the one before it, this much in percent.
A screen that holds each frame until the next (every 60 Hz LCD) smears whatever moves,
because the eye gets one picture per 16.7 ms; two pictures per frame (50 is a good value)
look like one picture per 8.3 ms and smear about half as much. The world keeps its pixels:
the moment nothing moves, current and previous frame are the same and the picture is fully
sharp. While things move, edges are softer \u2014 that is the trade. Call it before
`new Window`; 0 (the default) turns it off.

Creates a sprite for each object of a layer whose type names a sprite class,

methods.description:
Creates a sprite for each object of a layer whose type names a sprite class,
and adds it to the stage. In Tiled, give an object the type (called
"class" in newer versions of Tiled) `Player`, and the map makes a
`new Player()` where the object is.

The sprite's class needs one of these constructors, tried in this order:
one that takes the [MapObject](../MapObject/index) (to read its name and properties), one
that takes `(double x, double y)`, or one without parameters. Either
way the sprite is put where the object is. An object drawn as an area
(a rectangle, an ellipse or a polygon) also gives the sprite that area as
its hitbox, which is how walls and water work without a costume.

Objects whose type is not a sprite class, or that have no type, are left
alone, so a layer can hold markers the program reads itself.

```java
TiledMap map = new TiledMap("level.tmx", this);
map.spawn("Objects");
```
methods.returns: the sprites that were made, in the order of the layer
